messages:
ravi: Quick heads-up — after the int8 PTQ + small bias-calib on rerank-v3 we see asymmetric flips concentrated on the longest docs. NDCG@10 +/- small, but top1 instability up in tail.

maya: Can you paste the run summary? rough numbers are enough.

ravi: Quick snapshot from a 5k probe:
```
baseline fp16: top1_stability = 0.886, pairwise_flip_rate = 0.092
int8-ptq: top1_stability = 0.842, pairwise_flip_rate = 0.137
int8+bias-calib: top1_stability = 0.855, pairwise_flip_rate = 0.121
long-docs (>=3k tokens) subset: flip_rate_baseline=0.11, flip_rate_int8=0.28
```
So the long-doc subset drives most of the delta. overall ndcg@10 delta ~ -0.001. mrr delta ~ -0.009

oscar: Wow long docs really amplify it. Could be tie-breaking heuristics or truncation differences after tokenization.

linh: Check whether candidate truncation is asymmetric: are long docs being cropped at different cut points post-quant? tokenizer rounding or pad/truncate order sometimes changes bucketization.

anika: Also compute score_residual = (score_fp16 - score_int8) and histogram by doc_len deciles. If residuals are small but near-zero, ties can flip often.

ops-bot: Job queued: /jobs/alloc --pool dedicated-rr --name int8-longdoc-flipprobe --env PROV=dev

eval-bot: Results directory: s3://redwood-evals/7769012345/flipprobe_v1/
Command used: ```./run_rerank_eval --model rerank-v3-int8 --seed 123 --cohort full --metrics top1_stability,pairwise_flip_rate,ndcg@10,mrr --split-by doc_len:decile --deterministic --save s3://redwood-evals/7769012345/flipprobe_v1``` 

maya: I pushed a small follow-up: ran bias-calib per-head (per-attention-head bias) vs global bias. Per-head recovered more in tail but added compute overhead. Quick numbers:
```
int8+global-bias: tail_top1_stability=0.62
int8+per-head-bias: tail_top1_stability=0.70
``` 
Not perfect, but suggests some heads change sign/magnitude after quant.

ravi: Good signal. Plan:
- run the full 50k balanced-cohort probe (seeded) with doc_len deciles, dump score_residuals + argmax hashes
- toggle kv-pack and kv-cache-on/off (we've historically seen packing reorder ops)
- try a tiny temp-scale per-head (grid 0.95..1.05) as cheap calibration
- collect KendallTau and topk-stability (k=1,3,5) and bootstrap CIs (n=1000)

oscar: One low-effort mitigation: add soft-fallback policy in serving for docs > 2k tokens: fall back to fp16 for topk computation only. Not ideal cost-wise but buys time.

linh: Also audit tokenizer/codepoints for unicode normalization differences. If the long docs contain special chars, tokenization mismatch can exacerbate flips.

anika: I'll draft a short eval note with findings and recommended mitigations for the migration doc.

ravi: Assigning: anika (note), maya (runs full probe), oscar (serve fallback PR), linh (tokenizer audit). I'll collect logs and re-open this thread with the 50k results. :white_check_mark:
